messages:
aj: quick heads-up from the long-context perf run on staging: mem grows roughly linearly over a 4h run at 64k context, even with expected KV hit rates. :eyes:

aj: dug into the KV cache stats and heap profile — looks like fragmentation/hole accumulation between allocations, not just plain leaks. small free chunks piling up and not being stitched/reused.

aj: pasted kv diagnostics: 
```
kv_cache.stats() => 
live_blocks: 1248
free_chunks: 432
avg_free_chunk: 6.1KB
largest_free_run: 192KB
fragmentation_ratio: 0.39  # (sum_free / total_allocated)
page_ops.paged_out: 0
page_ops.paged_in: 0
```

aj: profiler (heap) shows repeated small alloc/free patterns localized to attention KV writes, interleaved with long-lived pinned segments (past kv-epoch pins).

maya: yup saw something similar on my replay of the customer workload. holes mostly between 8k and 64k. allocator currently uses a 16k base block size with power-of-two buckets; that granularity might be causing internal fragmentation for our variable kv-entry sizes.

liam: could we try a dual-path allocator? keep the current slab buckets for <32KB and a buddy/seglist for >32KB, plus coalescing of adjacent free runs. stitching free runs was missing in previous design for concurrency reasons.

sanjay: +1 on stitching. we intentionally avoided eager coalesce because compaction pauses were scary. but we could do opportunistic coalesce during background ticks and cap work by time budget. low-load compaction seems reasonable.

emily: what about tuning block_size to 32k or 64k? fewer blocks => fewer boundaries/holes, but might increase internal waste for tiny kvs. we need to measure tokenization distributions.

aj: tried a quick experiment: bumped base block to 32k on a dev instance and ran the same workload for 1h. RSS slope reduced ~30%, peak mem up slightly but steadier. tradeoff looks promising.

aj: snippet of the quick patch I ran (throwaway):
```python
# experimental patch
kv.cfg.base_block_size = 32 * 1024
kv.cfg.enable_background_coalesce = True
kv.cfg.coalesce_budget_ms = 5  # max ms per background tick
kv.cfg.compact_threshold = 0.65
```

liam: nice. does background_coalesce lock hot code paths? we need it lock-free or with shard-local locks to avoid stall on inference threads.

aj: I used shard-local background tasks so no global stop-the-world. still need to validate CPU overhead.

maya: another observation: reuse heuristic doesn't prefer adjacent free runs, it prefers first-fit. switching to best-fit-with-local-merge could reduce fragmentation. also add a fast-path to reuse a free chunk if size within 10% of requested.

sanjay: eviction/paging angle: when we evict pages we currently drop entire block ranges; that creates holes. Consider an eviction scheme that slices out just the least-recent KV entries and rewrites denser blocks to free contiguous ranges (compaction-on-evict). heavy I/O but bounded if we throttle it.

emily: curious about how this interacts with pinned KV during generation: long-context pinned ranges prevent compaction unless we snapshot remap. any ideas?

liam: we can implement a per-shard remap table: compaction creates a new compacted block and atomically swap pointers once ready, leaving pinned references to old blocks until they naturally retire. similar to GC moving collectors but simpler.

aj: that would avoid pauses. complexity up but seems doable.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: add feature flag for background_coalesce; add telemetry for fragmentation_ratio, coalesce_cpu_ms, compaction_ops, and remap_hits.

maya: action items: 1) aj open WIP PR with the base_block_size experiment + background coalesce (feature-flagged). 2) liam to prototype remap swap idea in a branch. 3) sanjay to sketch eviction-compaction flow and CPU/I/O budget model. 4) emily to run token-size distribution on 10 customer traces.

aj: I'll file the PR and include the perf logs and the 1h experiment config. planning a full 4h run tomorrow with 32k baseline and the feature flag on.

liam: small nits to measure: fragmentation_ratio over time, avg_free_chunk, median_free_chunk, compaction_cpu/ms, & tail-latency impact during background ops.

sanjay: we should also add a microbenchmark that allocates varying KV sizes in a realistic interleaving to reproduce the hole pattern deterministically. will help evaluate heuristics quickly.

emily: +1. also add a canary traffic suite to make sure remap swap doesn't regress latency p99.

aj: cool. i'll assign owners in the issue and drop links here once PR and benchmarks are up. thanks all :thumbsup:
